advice: The WHO 2021 air quality guideline for PM2.5 is a 24-hour mean of 15 ug/m3. Above this level, sensitive groups should reduce prolonged outdoor exertion.
The WHO 2021 air quality guideline for PM10 is a 24-hour mean of 45 ug/m3. On dusty days, keep windows closed and avoid roadside exercise.
People with asthma or COPD should carry their reliever inhaler, stay indoors when PM2.5 is high, and seek care if breathlessness worsens.
Exercise outdoors when pollution and heat are lowest. Move the workout indoors or shorten it when PM2.5 is well above the WHO guideline.
During a heatwave, drink water regularly even if you are not thirsty, avoid sugary or caffeinated drinks, and wear light, loose, light-coloured clothing.
Avoid going out in the hottest hours (roughly 12:00 to 16:00). If travel is unavoidable, use shade, an umbrella or cap, and carry water.
Children overheat quickly. Never leave them in parked vehicles, keep them hydrated, and pick them up from school in shade where possible.
Older people and those with heart disease are at higher risk. Check on them twice a day during a heatwave and keep their room cool and ventilated.
Outdoor workers should take frequent breaks in the shade, drink water every 15 to 20 minutes, and shift heavy work to early morning or evening.
Signs of heatstroke include confusion, a very high body temperature and hot dry skin. Move the person to shade, cool them with water and call emergency services (1122).
